decisions.executionNote: Approach the inner pair of upright supports with both arms in their own workspaces; establish continuous elbow-up reaching posture before final visual alignment.
Advance open grippers toward the inner two blocks, with a downward-forward grasp angle; use wrist views to refine pickup depth.
Make a small final forward/down correction, then close both grippers around the inner supports. Retention still needs a lift test.
Lift the two closed-gripper supports clear of the table and bring them toward symmetric lower-layer positions, checking that both blocks follow the wrists.
Lower both retained supports to table level at symmetric positions and open the grippers; inspect stability before moving the lower board.
Clear the released supports vertically, then move apart while turning the open grippers toward opposite-end board grasps; preserve configuration continuity.
Finish rotating both wrists into opposed board-grasp orientations above the long board. The released lower supports appear upright and symmetrically separated.
Lower both grippers to the long board's opposite ends and close symmetrically. A subsequent lift will test whether the board is retained.
Lift the long board evenly with both grippers closed, then begin shifting it rearward above the upright lower supports. Watch the board for tilt or slip.
Center the retained long board over the lower supports and lower it evenly toward contact. Keep both grippers closed until the board is seated.
Release the seated lower board, then withdraw both open grippers outward and upward without disturbing the supports.
The lower board remains across both supports after release. Move above the two remaining outer blocks and begin reorienting for individual upright grasps.
Align each wrist to its block's visible yaw and descend toward the grasp height with both grippers open; final depth and centering will be checked in wrist views.
Use wrist-image lateral offsets to center the outer blocks between the fingers, descend the last centimeter, then close both grippers for a lift test.
Lift both closed-gripper blocks clear of the lower board, straighten their yaw while keeping them upright, and begin bringing them inward. Verify both blocks follow the wrists.
Both blocks remain in the wrist views during the lift. Carry them inward above the lower board, keeping upright orientations and lateral separation for the middle supports.

Lower the retained middle supports over symmetric positions on the lower board. The right grasp sits farther forward in its wrist view, so use a slightly higher initial seating height and inspect before release.
Seat the middle supports gently, release both grippers, and lift clear. Small depth corrections center their footprints on the lower board; confirm upright placement as the wrists withdraw.
Both middle supports appear upright on the lower board. Move the open grippers toward the shorter board's ends while rotating to opposed board grasps.
Finish aligning the opposed grippers and approach the shorter board evenly, stopping above its pickup height for a final wrist-view check.
Descend the remaining distance to the shorter board and close both grippers symmetrically. Keep the board level and test retention with a vertical lift next.
Lift the shorter board evenly with both grippers closed to clear the middle supports, beginning rearward transport only after gaining height. Check for retention and tilt.
The shorter board followed the lift and appears level. Carry it rearward above the middle supports with fixed wrist orientations and symmetric motion.
Lower the centered shorter board evenly onto the middle supports, holding both grasps closed until seating is visually checked.
Open both grippers to release the seated middle board, then withdraw outward and upward. Inspect tower stability before collecting the two top pieces.
The middle board remains level after release. Approach the small wooden top board with the left arm and stage the right arm above the green top piece, rotating gradually to downward-forward grasps.
Complete the wrist alignment over both top pieces and descend cautiously, keeping the grippers open until the wrist views establish pickup centering.
Correct the small board's yaw and close the left grasp. Reorient the right gripper to approach the green roof from its side so the fingers contact the flat end faces rather than its slopes.
Lift-test the small wooden board in the closed left grasp, starting its quarter-turn only after clearance. Finish the right side approach and close around the green roof at table height.
The small board followed the left lift. Carry it inward above tower height while finishing its horizontal alignment; lift-test the closed right roof grasp without moving it over the tower yet.
Both top pieces remain in their wrist views after lifting. Center the small board over the middle layer and stage the roof safely to the right, keeping both closed grasps and upright orientations.
Apply a small visual centering correction and lower the small wooden board onto the middle board. Keep the roof parked to the right until the small board is released and stable.
The small board appears slightly right of the tower center. Lift minimally to recenter it left, reseat and release, then begin clearing the left gripper while the roof remains held aside.
The small board remains seated after opening. Withdraw the left arm clear of the tower first, then bring the retained green roof inward above the top board with the right arm.
Center the retained roof above the small board and lower toward seating. Start returning the clear, open left arm toward origin using gradual configuration-continuous motion.
Release the centered roof and withdraw the right gripper outward/upward. Continue the left arm toward its origin while watching that the full tower stays stable.
The full tower remains upright after roof release. Finish bringing the left arm to origin and move the open right arm away from the tower along a gradual return path.
Keep the stable tower untouched and both grippers open. Hold the left arm at origin while gradually lowering and reorienting the right arm along its own return path.
Complete the right arm's return to its initial pose with reduced final increments. Keep both grippers open and leave the visibly upright, centered tower undisturbed.
